tools/probe-child-death-codes.mjs.note: the measured answer to residue 2026-09-22-heap-retry-would-misdiagnose-enospc, which feared that a child killed by a FULL DISK aborts the way a heap death aborts — so trio-batch's isHeapOom would read it as a memory cap and retry the night at RETRY_HEAP_MB, the wrong remedy for a cause the retry cannot touch. The row gates its own fix on one real occurrence and none arrived, so this takes the third path: measure whether a disk fault can reach the code the predicate keys on at all. The instrument is /dev/full, which raises the kernel's own ENOSPC without root and without filling anything. Pre-stated criterion: the number of uncaught disk deaths reaching exit 134 must be 0, and one is enough to make the hazard real. Two controls, and a control that fails to establish itself makes the object UNKNOWN rather than a pass — a heap exhaustion under a 24 MB cap must abort with its own word (a probe blind to an abort would report the same zero), and a child that catches ENOSPC and calls process.exit(134) must be seen as 134 (a probe blind to a 134 would report it too). It does NOT import trio-batch, which has no exports and spawns children during module evaluation, and it does NOT re-implement the predicate: it reports the raw code, signal and word, while the predicate's own pins live in trio-batch --selftest over the strings measured here. The cmd is a sample object and probes nothing.
